title: Family life and his wife
summary: His wife has known him since age twelve and sacrifices for his career; family keeps him grounded.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Is it hard maintaining a family life with the travel you do?

I would say normally it is hard, but in my situation, again, I’m unique because my wife has known me since I was twelve years old, we grew up together, we’re the same age, so © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

she’s always seen me with a saxophone. So it’s not anything — now she had to get used to living with a saxophonist and the quirkiness of a jazz musician, but she never — she’s always seen me with a saxophone so that’s something that everyone that knows me, that knows us, says oh yeah, Javon has been playing the saxophone forever. So you still playing, yeah, you still playing the saxophone? Yeah. So that’s pretty constant, but then I have someone who is my partner who has been willing to sacrifice. Because in a relationship, when someone is doing really well or successful, at some point someone has to sacrifice for the sake of the family. And obviously when I get home from touring or whatever, I make what sacrifices I can to be there to help play catch-up to support that family. Because that’s a very important component to my maturity, is family life, and development as an artist, absolutely, is having a family, having them grounded, it creates and promotes humility. Because when you come home from that long tour in Japan, they want you to go down the street and get some more milk. So you need those kinds of things that are very grounding. Or, who’s going to wash the clothes this week? Or who’s going to sweep the floor? I mean general things. Sometimes we have someone do it. Sometimes we do it. So I appreciate those things that keep me humble.
